CHRONOLOGICAL SERVICE & DEPLOYMENT LOG

CLICK ANY MISSION LOG ENTRY TO EXPAND TACTICAL AFTER-ACTION NOTES

2940.08 — 2949.09 SEY

Entered the Officer Candidate Flight Pipeline at MacArthur Naval Base. Graduated in the top decile of her class with commendations in zero-G ballistic gunnery, decoupled drift vectors, and high-G energy management. Commissioned as Ensign (O-1) and selected for carrier interceptor track.

Assigned as wingman (Callsign: Bravo-Four) aboard the Bengal-class fleet carrier UEES Argus. Conducted continuous frontier border patrols along the Tiber and Virgil jump points, intercepting Vanduul harvester probes and smugglers running contraband into contested space.

Promoted to Lieutenant Junior Grade (LTJG). Flew 14 consecutive high-tempo defensive sorties in upper atmosphere and low orbit over New Corvo, screening civilian evacuation transports against Vanduul Hunter-class raiders during the surprise incursion.

Promoted to full Lieutenant (LT / O-3) and designated Bravo Flight Lead (214-Bravo-One). Spearheaded reconnaissance-in-force sweeps during the 65th Battle Group push into Oberon, logging 9 confirmed Vanduul Scythe and Glaive kills without losing a single flight wingman.

Classified deep-reconnaissance sweep near the Uriah jump perimeter. Bravo Flight was ambushed by cloaked Vanduul Void bomber escorts. Vance held a solo defensive screen for two crippled wingmen until Cutlass Red and Terrapin SAR units completed extraction; her Gladius took a direct plasma bolt through the lower port cockpit, severing her left leg below mid-thigh.

Completed 10 months of reconstructive neuro-vascular surgery and Type-IV Bio-Neural prosthetic integration. High-G centrifuge boards ruled LT Vance medically unfit for sustained 10G+ carrier interceptor duty. Honorably separated onto the Permanent Disability Retired List (PDRL) with full UEE Citizenship conferred.

01 // BALLISTIC & THERMAL TRAUMA

A Vanduul plasma bolt penetrated the lower port fuselage of LT Vance's Aegis Gladius, severing the primary hydraulic conduit and driving superheated shrapnel through the cockpit footwell. Her left leg was crushed and severed below mid-thigh with acute thermal nerve destruction and localized cockpit depressurization.

02 // IBRAHIM SPHERE NON-TRIGGER

Automated flight-suit tourniquet cuffs sealed the upper thigh and preserved life signs for 22 minutes until Cutlass Red and Terrapin SAR teams extracted her cockpit pod. Because clinical death never occurred, her Ibrahim Sphere imprint did not trigger a bio-print. Surgeons fitted a Type-IV Bio-Neural Prosthetic Limb (matte-titanium frame with synthetic dermal sheath).

03 // HIGH-G DISQUALIFICATION

Standard mobility and 1G flight reflexes tested at 98% of biological baseline. However, Naval Centrifuge Trials proved that sustained 9G–12G interceptor maneuvers caused severe vascular swelling, blood pooling, and neural feedback lag at the living residual-limb socket—mandating permanent carrier disqualification.
